items.question: Registered users are numerous, but the service sees only a modest request rate. What must a capacity estimate include besides user count?
A team says the system must be both fast and durable. How should that preference become a testable quality requirement?
A client times out after sending a write and retries. The server cannot tell whether the first attempt committed. How can it avoid applying the effect twice?
When should a business capability stay a module inside one deployable instead of becoming its own service?
Adding worker threads made tail latency worse instead of raising throughput. What saturation effect should be investigated first?
What actually limits a producer when a consumer applies backpressure, and where can blocking still escape that limit?
A service commits a database change and then publishes to a broker. How can it avoid losing the event if the process dies between those operations?
A consumer commits an offset and then crashes after performing an external side effect. Why can the side effect still repeat?
Two transactions each read a consistent snapshot, yet together they violate a business rule. What anomaly is this, and where should the fix live?
An index speeds up one query but slows another. What evidence should be collected before keeping or removing it?
A hot tenant must move to a new shard while writes continue. What can go wrong, and what must the migration prove before cutover?
A popular cache entry expires and many clients miss at once. What mechanism prevents every request from rebuilding the same value?
When should retrieval prefer a lexical ranker over embeddings for exact API names, error codes and version strings?
Why can an approximate nearest-neighbor index return a different top-k after a rebuild, and what should be measured before trusting it?
Throughput is stable but backlog grows. What does Little’s Law imply about residence time, and which boundary must be measured?
Why can automatic retries during overload delay recovery instead of helping it?
A column changes meaning while old and new application versions run. What must the migration prove before the old version is removed?
After a regional failover, two sites have accepted writes. How should the team reconcile them without silently choosing a winner?
How does trace context cross an asynchronous message boundary, and what can a missing span fail to prove?
What is the difference between an SLO and an error budget, and what should a budget breach trigger?
When is an incremental transition safer than a big-bang replacement, and what must the transition state own?
Which mechanism makes a receiver safe when the broker can deliver the same message more than once?

One description says Kafka transactions make an end-to-end workflow exactly-once; another says they only cover Kafka reads and writes. Which claim is defensible, and what remains outside the guarantee?
A cache TTL is shortened to reduce staleness. Which load, origin-protection and correctness checks must be rerun?
A shared serialization library is upgraded across services. Which caller and server compatibility evidence is required before rollout?
An SLO target is tightened. What alerts, budget actions and operational expectations must change with it?
A primary-key type changes on a large table. Which compatibility, backfill and replication checks are affected?
A service moves from VMs to containers. Which placement, runtime and observability assumptions must be revalidated?
One page treats replicas as extra read capacity; another shows that more replicas can increase contention. When is each claim true?
A cache is described as a scalability layer and as a consistency risk. How should both claims be scoped?
Autoscaling is presented as overload protection and as a source of instability. What determines which effect dominates?
Strong quorum consistency is said to cost availability and to prevent divergent authority. Which failure envelope makes both statements compatible?
Retries use jitter, yet clients still arrive in synchronized bursts. What else must the retry policy control?
A leader election finishes, but two nodes briefly accept writes. Which safety mechanism failed?
A canary shows healthy host metrics while users report errors. Which acceptance boundary was wrong?
A failover loses recent writes even though replication was configured as synchronous. What must be verified about acknowledgement scope?
When is a strongly consistent quorum worth its latency and availability cost?
When is a shared database between two services an acceptable boundary, and what must be made explicit?
When is a serverless compute model a poor fit for a latency-sensitive service?
When is denormalization justified in a read-heavy system, and what consistency cost must be accepted?
How do idempotency, an outbox and consumer offsets combine into one end-to-end duplicate-safe workflow?
How do SLOs, load-test evidence and capacity models combine into a launch gate?
How do schema evolution and rolling deployment constrain each other during a semantic change?
How do tenancy, authorization and caching interact on a multi-tenant read path?
What does a fencing token prevent after a lease or leadership change?
What is the difference between RTO and RPO, and what evidence turns each into a measured objective?
What does a circuit breaker add beyond a per-request timeout?
What does a watermark mean in event-time stream processing, and what does it not guarantee?
What does a bulkhead isolate, and which failure does it fail to prevent?
A stakeholder asks for a scalable design but cannot name the outcome that matters. Which artifact should turn the concern into testable scenarios and readable views?
Two teams draw different diagrams of the same system. What should a description contract require so the views can be compared?
A design depends on an external identity provider. What authority and dependency facts must be recorded before calling it a boundary?
A team wants to prove a design choice with a benchmark. What makes an architecture experiment discriminating rather than decorative?
An internal event is published before the database commit. What timing failure does this create, and where should the boundary move?
A legacy API returns status codes that do not match the new domain model. Where should translation live, and what must not leak across the boundary?
A tenant identifier is present in the request but missing from a cache key. What isolation failure is possible?
A caller sets a two-second timeout and retries twice. What end-to-end budget must be enforced, and by whom?
A module boundary exists only in documentation. What enforcement evidence would make it real?
Virtual threads improve throughput in one service but not another. What workload property explains the difference?
A reactive pipeline blocks on a database driver and loses its scheduler context. What symptom and fix should be expected?
A latency regression appears only in production. What discriminating runtime experiment should run before changing the pool size?
Two tasks update shared state without a transaction. Which invariant can break, and where must enforcement live?
A reactive endpoint returns success while the consumer falls behind. How does demand propagate, and where can it be lost?
A producer increases Kafka partitions to raise throughput. Which ordering and consumer-contract assumptions change?
A workflow needs delayed retries, ordering and replay. Which messaging family fits, and what must be verified?
Two offline clients edit the same record and sync later. One policy says last-write-wins; another says preserve both. What must be made explicit before merging?
A leader change completes, but a client still reads stale data from the old leader. What session or lease rule was violated?
A long-running report holds an old snapshot while disk usage grows. Which MVCC lifetime mechanism is involved?
An index helps the benchmark query but hurts the mixed workload. What controlled validation should decide whether to keep it?
A team adds a document store beside PostgreSQL for one feature. What synchronization and authority costs must be compared?
A tenant key range becomes hot after a promotion. What resharding and fencing steps prevent double writes?
A column is retired, but old rows still contain meaningful data. What lifecycle and retention checks precede removal?
A cache refresh fails and a stale value is served. Who owns regeneration, and what bound makes the stale read acceptable?
A search cluster updates documents asynchronously. How can a citation point to a version the user can no longer see?
A local cache in every instance disagrees after an update. Which authority and invalidation model should be chosen?
A hybrid ranker improves recall but lowers citation precision. What evaluation must decide whether to keep it?
An exact error code is split by the tokenizer. Which indexing choice preserves it?
A load test shows a 20 percent improvement after a client change. Which confounders must be controlled before believing it?
An open-loop generator reports lower throughput than a closed-loop one. Which model matches the user arrival process?
A queue looks stable in a five-minute window but grows over an hour. What measurement boundary explains the contradiction?
A design meets peak throughput but doubles idle cost. What capacity envelope and cost comparison should be required?
A load balancer removes an instance on a failed health check while requests are in flight. What routing and draining contract is missing?
A pod receives a termination signal and closes connections immediately. Which client retry and idempotency assumptions are exposed?
A cell failure takes out ten percent of tenants. How do cells and shuffle sharding bound the blast radius?
A canary passes error-rate checks but corrupts shared state. What acceptance signal was missing?
A disaster-recovery test restores data but takes twice the target time. What RTO evidence is still missing?
A metrics label contains user IDs and cardinality explodes. What retention and aggregation decision should be made?
An agent can query a knowledge service but must not read another tenant documents. What trust boundary and authorization check are required?
An incident review lists a root cause but no detection gap. What practice evidence should be added?
Two tenants share a database and a connection pool. Which isolation dimensions must be tested separately?
An audit log records that a change happened but not who authorized it. What lineage and audit fields are missing?
A modernization decision record compares two vendors but omits the transition state. What is missing from the decision?
A team wants to rewrite a monolith because it is hard to change. What baseline evidence should precede that decision?
A legacy system behavior is known only from operator anecdotes. What observation baseline is required before migration?
A pattern is recommended without a contraindication. What applicability evidence should the card require?
Should a bounded capability remain one deployable with enforced module boundaries, rather than split into independently deployed services?
Should models and ownership be separated by bounded context rather than forced into one shared enterprise model?
Should responsibilities be grouped into layers with an enforced dependency direction, rather than organized around ports or independently deployed services?
Should dependencies point inward toward domain policies, with frameworks and delivery mechanisms at the outside?
Should a service reduce synchronous dependencies by owning or duplicating the data and behavior it needs, rather than calling other services on every request?
Should external clients enter through a managed gateway that owns routing, authentication and cross-cutting edge policy?
Should a gateway aggregate several downstream responses into one client-facing result, rather than making the client orchestrate every call?
Should each client population get a tailored server contract, rather than share one general-purpose API?
Should callers resolve backend instances through a discovery mechanism rather than static addresses?
Should a proxy or load balancer own service lookup and backend selection for the caller?
Should one event reach all interested subscribers without the publisher knowing their count?
Should multiple consumers share one queue to scale processing and smooth bursts?
Should related messages carry an explicit identifier so replies and follow-ups can be matched?
Should messages be removed when they do not meet explicit criteria?
Should a composite message be divided into independently processed parts?
Should messages that cannot be processed be isolated in a dead-letter channel?
Should the receiver detect duplicate deliveries and avoid duplicate effects?
Should a broker mediate routing and delivery between producers and consumers, possibly bridging protocols?
Should a durable coordinator or a routing-slip itinerary own a multi-step message flow and its recovery?
Should authoritative state be derived from an ordered event history rather than stored as current rows?
Should saga participants react to events without a central coordinator?
Should a failed saga step be undone by an explicit business compensation rather than a rollback?
Should a client-supplied key let the server recognize retries of one logical request?
Should a query result be stored and refreshed explicitly rather than recomputed per request?
Should cached data live in a shared distributed tier rather than only inside each process?
Should the cache layer load missing data on behalf of the application?
Should writes land in the cache first and reach the store asynchronously?
Should entries expire after a bounded time even without an explicit invalidation?
Should concurrent misses be coordinated so they do not all hit the source at once?
Should data be cached in more than one tier with different latency and freshness?
Should data be split across shards by a partition key to scale beyond one node?
Should keys and nodes share a hash ring so membership changes move only a fraction of data?
Should read-only replicas serve queries to offload the writer?
Should a separate lookup table maintain a secondary access path?
Should data be backfilled while the system continues serving reads and writes?
Should different data responsibilities use different stores while one authoritative boundary owns consistency?
Should a failed call be retried after increasing delays?
Should each call have a bounded wait before it is treated as failed?
Should a failed primary path return a defined degraded result?
Should request rate be limited to protect a dependency or budget?
Should work be buffered in a queue so producers and consumers can run at different rates?
Should an external monitor distinguish liveness, readiness and startup health?
Should one node be chosen to coordinate work while others stand by?
Should a shared lock prevent concurrent access to one resource across processes?
Should decisions require a majority of replicas rather than one node?
Should one client session preserve selected read/write observations across replicas?
Should capacity be added by running more instances rather than a larger instance?
Should capacity be adjusted automatically from observed or predicted demand?
Should independent deployment units be replicated as stamps for scale, isolation or locality?
Should static content be served from a dedicated store or edge rather than the application origin?
Should instances be replaced incrementally while traffic continues?
Should activation be decoupled from deployment through a runtime toggle?
Should infrastructure be replaced rather than mutated in place?
Should old and new implementations process the same work concurrently for comparison?
Should a schema change be rolled out in expand, migrate and contract stages?
Should identity be asserted by a trusted issuer and accepted across services, rather than locally re-authenticated?
Should access be decided by roles or attributes rather than ad hoc checks?
Should a client receive a scoped, time-limited credential for direct resource access?
Should logs be emitted as structured events with stable fields rather than free text?
Should service health be governed by user-visible indicators, objectives and an explicit error budget?
In the cache-aside pattern, what does an application do on a cache hit and on a cache miss, and how does this differ from read-through caching?
Under cache-aside, how is cached data invalidated when a record is updated, and what consistency gap can remain?
What does a time-to-live (TTL) value accomplish in a cache-aside design, and what trade-off determines whether it is too short or too long?
Why can a popular cached item produce a cache stampede when its TTL expires, even if request volume has not increased?
How does request coalescing or a per-key cache lock prevent a stampede, and what can requests that do not acquire the lock do?

A service handles a long-run average of 250 requests per second, and each request spends an average of 120 ms in the system. Using Little's law, what is the average number of requests in the system, and what condition must hold for the law to apply?

A team inserts a queue between a bursty producer and a consumer that processes at a fixed rate. What does the producer now wait for, and what happens if the producer's long-run average rate stays above the consumer's? Name two responses the Azure guidance recommends.
In Reactive Streams, which side controls the pace of element delivery, what limit must a Publisher respect, and why must the demand signal be non-blocking?

A request path is five service layers deep, and each layer retries a failed call three times. What load amplification can the deepest dependency see, and how do exponential backoff with jitter and retry limits reduce it?

A five-server Raft cluster uses majority quorums. How many server failures can it tolerate while still electing a leader and committing new entries, and what property of majorities keeps two partitions from both making progress?

A Raft leader is cut off by a network partition and never learns that a new leader was elected. Why can the isolated leader not commit new log entries, and what stops it from corrupting committed history?
Why can a leased distributed lock fail to protect a shared resource when its holder pauses, and how does a fencing token close that gap?
ZooKeeper's administrator guide recommends odd-sized ensembles. What does a four-server ensemble actually tolerate, and why does the fourth server add little?
Under RFC 9110, which request methods are idempotent, and when may a client automatically retry a request whose method is not idempotent?
Which retry controls does Google's SRE book recommend to prevent retry amplification, and what multiplication example illustrates the risk?
Why is publishing to a message broker inside a database transaction unreliable, and how does the transactional outbox pattern avoid that problem?
How does the idempotent consumer pattern detect a duplicate message, and why is the processed-messages primary key important?
In a MongoDB sharded cluster, how do the shard key and chunk layout govern query routing and rebalancing, and why can hashed sharding help with a monotonically increasing key?
What distinguishes head-based from tail-based trace sampling, and why can head sampling alone fail to retain every trace that contains an error?
Which three model families does V12 use, and what does each represent?
What must a V12 model specification declare before a run?
How does V12 keep source, calibration and simulation evidence separate?
When is stock-and-flow the right abstraction instead of discrete-event simulation?
Why does a queued request consume a retry attempt in V12?
How is a stored V12 run bound to its model, scenario and engine?
What makes the checkout B recommendation conditional rather than universal?
Why is the modernization cutover decision insufficient-evidence?
How does a V12 decision link to existing pattern owner pages without editing them?
Which gates must V12 simulation evidence pass before a decision uses it?
How do convergence and replication count affect a Monte Carlo result?
What changes when the sensitivity screen must handle correlated inputs?
What are the limits of the staged modernization simulation?
How can an external agent go from a pattern ID to V12 simulation artifacts?
